business.title: Assessment of solar organic rankine cycle systems for power generation in Nigeria
business.desc: Nigeria has abundant solar energy, especially in the north, which is underexploited. The solar organic Rankine cycle (solar ORC) converts low- to medium-temperature heat sources into electricity or heat. This study analyses the deployment of solar ORC systems in Nigeria, employing an evacuated tube collector (ETC) as the main heat source, focusing on the impact of regional heat sources on performance parameters, net power output, thermal efficiency, heat input, and turbine and pump work output. This study demonstrates a region-by-region comparison approach that integrates Nigeria’s solar energy resources with solar ORC performance. Six regions with heat source temperatures from 100 to 140 °C were analysed using R245fa. Direct normal irradiance data determined the regions’ highest solar potential. The northwest (140 °C) and northeast (135 °C) achieve the highest net power (47 and 48 kW) with cycle efficiencies of 18–19%. In the south-south (100 °C), net power drops to 37 kW, efficiency is 15%, turbine work is 38 kW, and pump work is 0.8 kW. Predicted efficiencies were consistent with previous studies reported in the literature. Net power, efficiency, and turbine work increase with heat source temperature. Future research should focus on site-specific studies to support technical viability before real-world applications.

technology.title: An integrated methodology and sensitivity analysis for the prediction and multiobjective optimization of the thermophysical properties of MWCNT/water nanofluids using SVR-GA and SPEA2
technology.desc: This study proposes an integrated methodology that utilizes intelligent computing to precisely predict and optimize the thermophysical properties of a three-dimensional multi-walled carbon nanotube (MWCNT)/water nanofluid. Two distinct Support Vector Regression (SVR) models, enhanced by hyperparameter optimization using a Genetic Algorithm (GA), were successfully trained to accurately estimate the dynamic viscosity (DV) and thermal conductivity (TC) based on experimental data across a range of volume concentrations (0–0.5%) and temperatures (30–65 °C). The resulting SVR-GA models demonstrated high predictive accuracy, evidenced by the test data’s mean and maximum relative percentage errors: 0.4546% and 0.9690% for DV, and 0.5950% and 0.9532% for TC, respectively. Moreover, the trained SVR models have been validated using K-fold cross-validation, and the network’s accuracy in estimating unseen data has been demonstrated. A sensitivity analysis confirmed that temperature exerts a greater influence on nanofluid properties than volume concentration. Leveraging these high-accuracy models, a multiobjective optimization problem was formulated to simultaneously minimize DV and maximize TC. This problem was solved using the Strength Pareto Evolutionary Algorithm 2 (SPEA2), which yielded a Pareto front of optimal trade-off solutions. The analysis of the Pareto front consistently identified 65 °C as the optimal operating temperature, providing useful insights for selecting conditions that maximize the nanofluid’s heat transfer efficiency.

technology.title: Operational risk assessment of distribution networks considering electric vehicle V2G strategies
technology.desc: Large-scale EV integration changes both when and where load appears in distribution networks, which makes nodal voltage and branch power flow more vulnerable to concentrated demand. This study develops an operational risk assessment framework for distribution networks under EV V2G strategies. An EV spatiotemporal charging/discharging model is first built from trip-chain behavior and dynamic state-of-charge evolution, and two V2G modes are then described: a fixed-schedule strategy and a risk-guided strategy. On that basis, a probabilistic power flow model is established to capture the uncertainty of distributed generation, conventional demand, and EV behavior. Weighted distribution entropy is employed to represent explicit risks associated with voltage and branch-flow limit violations, while Theil entropy is introduced to measure the unevenness of state-variable changes, and the two are combined into a comprehensive risk index. Simulations on a modified IEEE 33-bus system under three operating scenarios show that the proposed method can clearly track how operational risk evolves over time under different V2G strategies. Among the compared cases, the risk-guided V2G strategy provides the most effective peak-risk suppression and delivers a smoother risk profile during critical periods.
